claims.claim: David Hartlage quotes Bob Bledsaw in Dragon 27 saying judges regarded describing dungeons as their own domain.
claims.source: Bob Bledsaw in Dragon #27, quoted by David Hartlage, DMDavid, 2016
claims.quote: judges felt that the actual description of dungeons was their ‘domain’
claims.page: How much description, 'Tegel Manor and minimal descriptions'

claims.claim: Luke Gearing's rewrite of his own adventure consisted largely of turning its bullet points back into prose.
claims.source: Luke Gearing, 'Bullet Points vs Prose', lukegearing.blot.im, 2023
claims.quote: A lot of this involves de-bullet pointing the text.

claims.claim: Luke Gearing says his own bullet points were already more prose-based than most, which worsens rather than eases his objection to them.
claims.source: Luke Gearing, 'Bullet Points vs Prose', lukegearing.blot.im, 2023
claims.quote: I find this only exacerbates my issue with them.

claims.claim: Luke Gearing's model prose keys a room in the present tense from a single dominant smell or object outward.
claims.source: Luke Gearing's own demonstration passage, 'Bullet Points vs Prose', 2023
claims.quote: The smell of cold grease fills the air
claims.page: Bullet Points vs Prose, room 4 Kitchen, prose version

claims.claim: Luke Gearing's method for writing a place is to close his eyes and imagine standing in it.
claims.source: Luke Gearing, 'Techniques to Write Adventures', lukegearing.blot.im, 2021
claims.quote: I often just close my eyes and imagine being there

claims.claim: Luke Gearing says that mental walk-through is for finding the touchstones that communicate a place's tone.
claims.source: Luke Gearing, 'Techniques to Write Adventures', lukegearing.blot.im, 2021
claims.quote: finding those touchstones which communicate the tone

claims.claim: Zach Howard judges the introduction to the Holmes Basic Sample Dungeon highly evocative, reading almost like weird fiction.
claims.source: Zach Howard (Zenopus Archives), 'Part 46: "Zenopus Built a Tower"', 2015
claims.quote: The introduction is highly evocative, reading almost like the weird fiction

claims.claim: J. Eric Holmes instructs the Dungeon Master to read the sample dungeon's background material aloud to the assembled players.
claims.source: J. Eric Holmes, D&D Basic Set (1977), quoted by Zach Howard (Zenopus Archives) 2015
claims.quote: should read the background material above to the assembled players

claims.claim: Howard reads Holmes's Portown background as material meant to be read to the players, predating boxed text.
claims.quote: this background material is meant to be read to the players

claims.claim: Howard calls Holmes's one-paragraph account of Portown's trade, ships and inhabitants a thumbnail sketch of a campaign setting.
claims.quote: Here we get a thumbnail sketch of a campaign setting

claims.claim: Delta dates the first boxed text in a Gygax adventure to the 1982 published Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', Delta's D&D Hotspot, 2021
claims.quote: And hey, there's boxed text for the first time!
claims.page: section '1982 - Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth Publication'

claims.claim: Gygax's 1974 Castle Greyhawk notes gave a single curt bullet-line per encounter area.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area

claims.claim: In the 1978 Steading of the Hill Giant Chief the area paragraphs tend to lead with sense-descriptions.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: the paragraphs tend to lead with those sense-descriptions
claims.page: section '1978 - Steading of the Hill Giant Chief'

claims.claim: Expedition to the Barrier Peaks devotes almost 500 words to the Ship Commander's Quarters, an area with no monsters.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: almost 500 words total for the one area
claims.page: section '1980 - Expedition to the Barrier Peaks'

claims.claim: Isle of the Ape opens with a boxed speech by Tenser of some 1,600 words to be read verbatim.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: 2 full pages of text to be read verbatim
claims.page: section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'
